results.title: India Anti-Drug Operation: Operation Trident Busts International Drug Cartel, 18 Arrested, 1,424 Accounts Frozen
results.description: The Indian government has announced a major breakthrough in its crackdown on drug trafficking with Operation Trident, a coordinated action targeting an international narcotics cartel operating across India's northeastern region. Union Home Minister Amit Shah shared details of the operation on social media, highlighting the agencies' efforts to dismantle the alleged trafficking network and disrupt its financial operations. According to the information shared by Shah, multiple agencies conducted simultaneous raids on October 23 across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur. The coordinated action reportedly covered 38 locations and resulted in the dismantling of an international narcotics cartel. Authorities also uncovered suspected hawala transactions worth approximately ₹100 crore, indicating the scale of the financial network allegedly linked to the operation. As part of the crackdown, 1,424 bank accounts were frozen and 18 people were arrested. The action is aimed at disrupting both the supply chain and the financial infrastructure that allegedly supported the trafficking activities. Investigators reportedly found that the network used what was described as the “Death Triangle Corridor” to smuggle narcotics across the borders of India, Myanmar and Bangladesh. The region's cross-border routes have long posed challenges for law enforcement agencies seeking to prevent the movement of illegal drugs and dismantle organised trafficking networks. The operation highlights the government's focus on coordinated enforcement, financial investigations and intelligence-led action against drug syndicates. By freezing bank accounts and identifying suspected hawala transactions, agencies are seeking to target the money flows that can sustain international narcotics operations.
